Bluetooth

The Mini Program encapsulates the Bluetooth capability of each platform through a unified interface for developers to use. Using the Bluetooth interface of the Mini Program, developers can exchange data with other Bluetooth devices wirelessly.

1. Bluetooth Capability Overview

Bluetooth technical specifications are formulated by the Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG). Developers can obtain detailed technical documents from the official website. Currently, the most commonly used Bluetooth specifications are as follows:

  • Bluetooth Base Rate/Enhanced Data Rate (Bluetooth Basic Rate/Enhanced Data Rate, BR/EDR): is also known as Classic Bluetooth. It is usually used in scenarios that have certain requirements on data transmission bandwidth, such as Bluetooth speakers and Bluetooth headsets that need to transmit audio data.
  • Bluetooth low energy (Bluetooth Low Energy, BLE): a protocol supported since Bluetooth 4.0, characterized by extremely low power consumption and a higher transmission speed, and usually used in various intelligent electronic products that have a relatively high requirement on a battery life and need to transmit only a small amount of data. such as smart wearables, smart appliances, sensors, devices, etc., a wide range of application scenarios.

2. Bluetooth capability in the Mini Program

In the Mini Program, to use the Bluetooth capability, you must first call ma.openBluetoothAdapter to initialize the Bluetooth adapter module. The validity period is from the time when ma.openBluetoothAdapter is called to the time when ma.closeBluetoothAdapter is called or the Mini Program is destroyed. Only the When the Mini Program Bluetooth adapter module takes effect, developers can call Bluetooth-related Mini Program APIs and receive event callbacks related to the Bluetooth module (binding listening is not restricted).

The support of the Mini Program for Bluetooth is as follows:

  • Classic Bluetooth: not supported currently
  • Bluetooth low energy Device：
    • central mode: The basic library Macle 24.6.0 and later versions support this mode
    • peripheral mode: not supported currently
    • Beacon: not supported currently。

3. Precautions

Because the implementation and restrictions of the Bluetooth protocol stack vary greatly on different platforms, developers need to pay attention to the following aspects when using the Bluetooth capability of the Mini Program：

3.1 Device Id

Each Bluetooth peripheral device is identified by a unique deviceId. Due to the limitations of some systems, the deviceId obtained by scanning the same Bluetooth peripheral device on different central devices may be different. Therefore, deviceId cannot be hard-coded.

  • The deviceId obtained by scanning on the Android device is the MAC address of the peripheral device, which is relatively fixed.
  • The deviceId obtained by scanning the iOS device is the UUID generated by the system based on the MAC address of the peripheral device and the time when the device is discovered. For devices that have already been connected, the UUID remains unchanged for a period of time. In addition, the UUID may change under certain conditions, such as system The UUID obtained on different devices is different when the Bluetooth module is restarted or the paired device is ignored.

3.2 Debug

Bluetooth implementations also vary widely across platforms. On the basis of providing a unified interface, the Mini Program provides complete system Bluetooth capabilities as much as possible to weaken the implementation differences between different platforms.

However, due to the limitations of the operating system, some capabilities cannot be ensured to be completely consistent. Developers need to pay attention to the precautions in the document and debug the capabilities on real devices at each end. The developer tool can simulate only some Bluetooth interface capabilities. Use a real device to debug the complete functions.
